source_pack.canonical_content_text:
PJM peaked at 162.6 gigawatts (GW) on July 2, 2026, 1.3% higher than the pre-2026 peak of 160.6 GW on June 23, 2025. The Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) peaked at 91.1 GW on July 22, 2026, 6.5% higher than the pre-2026 record of 85.5 GW on August 20, 2024. The Southwest Power Pool (SWPP) peaked at 58.0 GW on July 27, 2026, 3.5% higher than the pre-2026 peak of 56.0 GW on August 21, 2023.

Data from Form EIA-930 is reported to us by each balancing authority (BA) and is made available "as-is". The data BAs report on the Form EIA-930 represent best values at the time of reporting, but various reporting issues may limit the quality of these data . Data published directly by BAs may differ from the data in Form EIA-930.

We estimate that U.S. generation from small-scale or rooftop solar photovoltaic systems (smaller than 1 megawatt of capacity) has increased from 18,812 gigawatthours (GWh) to 92,979 GWh over the last decade.
